source_read: PDF, Science 335: 601-604 (PDF pages 2-5; page 1 is the publisher's cover sheet): all running text, Fig. 1 and Fig. 2 legends, acknowledgments and notes; Fig. 1A, Fig. 1C and Fig. 2A-C checked on rendered pages (110 and 300 dpi). The Supporting Online Material is not in the PDF and was not read.

key_findings.note: Fig. 1A read at 300 dpi: about 239, 277 and 280 ms, as the card says. The asterisks mark only the two comparisons with the volunteers; no test between the two sibling groups is shown.
Fig. 1C plots all participants in one colour, consistent with a pooled correlation. The region of interest was chosen inside the skeleton of group differences (Fig. 1B legend); see missed.

Checked on the rendered p. 603: blue ventral frontal and insular clusters in Fig. 2A without counterparts in Fig. 2B, and large red posterior-fossa clusters in Fig. 2B. Also visible (editors' reading): the medial temporal enlargement is bilateral in Fig. 2A but left-sided only in Fig. 2B.
Whole report searched: methamphetamine is never named, and cocaine appears only in a sentence about preclinical research (p. 604).

reporting_issues.note: 141 error degrees of freedom equal 144 participants only for a one-way model without covariates, and the main report does not state the model. Covariates would also lower the df, but six would be needed; the identical df for SSRT and FA point to one analysed set of 144.
0.24 squared is 0.0576; the printed 0.057 fits an unrounded r near 0.239. With 144 participants r = 0.24 gives t of about 2.95 (p about 0.004), consistent with P < 0.005.

Partly a matter of reading: the familial putamen (striatal) and right inferior frontal white-matter (frontal) findings do fit 'fronto-striatal'. The overreach is that the shared amygdala, insular, postcentral and superior temporal differences are not fronto-striatal.
The discussion also describes the medial temporal lobe as a learning-and-memory system (p. 603, 8th paragraph, citing ref. 24), which invites a hippocampal reading that no named cluster supports.
Six tests counted: SSRT 0.033, FA skeleton 0.004, right prefrontal FA 0.004, putamen 0.013, posterior insula 0.012, amygdala 0.144; 0.05/6 = 0.0083.

risk_of_bias.note: Overall high agreed. ROBINS-E allows high when several domains with some concerns together substantially lower confidence, which is the card's reasoning; with confounding at high (domain note below), high also follows from the worst-domain rule. Provisional, as the card says, because the supplement was not read.

risk_of_bias_domains.note: Smoking was significantly more common in the sibling pairs than in the volunteers (p. 602, 3rd paragraph), and the main report checks it only for grey matter (p. 603, fig. S1). For the headline SSRT and FA differences, which the non-dependent siblings share, smoking is not controlled, and alcohol and other drug use, sex and education are not reported. Under ROBINS-E, an important confounder left uncontrolled that could plausibly change the result gives high; some concerns requires that the uncontrolled confounders be unlikely to matter. Provisional: if the supplement shows adjustment, some concerns would stand. The overall judgment is high either way.
Six of 150 missing by the degrees of freedom, with the model caveat in reporting issue 0.
Confirmed on the rendered Fig. 2A-B (see key finding 8).

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial agreed. One addition: the authors themselves write that reduced FA went with longer stimulant use, suggesting white-matter changes can also result from drug-taking (p. 602, 5th paragraph), one paragraph before they call the right prefrontal FA finding an objective vulnerability marker (6th paragraph). Their own data thus qualify the marker reading.

missed: Familiality test (p. 602, 4th-6th paragraphs; p. 603, 7th paragraph): true sibling pairs are compared with randomly re-paired siblings. Siblings are closer to each other in age than random pairs and share ethnicity and upbringing, and age strongly affects FA, grey-matter volume and SSRT; the main report does not say whether age was removed before the test or how the random pairs were drawn. Part of the 'familial' similarity may therefore be shared age and environment, which weakens the endophenotype reading further than the card's genes-versus-environment point.

Possible circular selection (Fig. 1B legend, p. 602): F(2,141) = 26.3 is given for 'the skeleton of group differences', and the right inferior frontal region for the FA-SSRT regression was selected inside that skeleton. If the F was computed on voxels chosen because they differed between groups, the editors' eta-squared of about 0.27 for FA is inflated, and the pooled FA-SSRT correlation inherits both the voxel selection and the group differences. The main report does not say which; the editors' FA eta-squared should carry this caveat.

Interests (p. 604): T.W.R. and A.J.T. consult for Cambridge Cognition, which (editors' background knowledge, not stated in the paper) sells computerized cognitive tests that include a stop-signal task; the main report does not say which stop-signal implementation was used. A flag for closer reading only.
